messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - RDMA link flaps on rack-7 causing serving errors (see alert id PD-9821) :rotating_light:
jasper: seeing lots of container restarts on serve-rt in rack-7, GPU OOM followed by CUDA driver reset on a few nodes. 50% of requests to model-x hitting 5xxs
maria: confirmed. netstat/ibstat shows frequent link down/up on hca3 across 3 nodes. packet retransmits spike before crash
devon: logs from one host: ```kernel: mlx5_core: InfiniBand device link state changed to DOWN
nvidia: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
serve-rt: ERROR: cuda runtime error: out of memory at kvstore.cc:122```
sre-lead: priority: page, mitigate customers first. @prod-support what customer impact do we have? any paid tenants hitting errors?
prod-support: telemetry: model-x error_rate -> 4.8% (baseline 0.2%), increased lat from 120ms -> 650ms for a subset routed to rack-7. A couple of small customers reported degraded responses, no major customers on Dedicated in that rack as far as I can see.
jasper: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable RDMA for serving pods on affected nodes (force TCP fallback) 2) drain one node at a time from K8s, restart serve-rt after driver / ib restart 3) apply kernel param tcp_retries2=8 to shorten stuck flows
maria: +1 on TCP fallback. runtime has automatic fallback but it's slow to detect link flaps which causes OOM because KV cache tries to sync across nodes. I'll push a quick hotfix to reduce kv cache sync window to 50ms (non-breaking)
devon: command I'm running on node-7a to force TCP: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
modprobe -r mlx5_ib && modprobe mlx5_ib transport_type=1```  (will do one node at a time)
jasper: doing node-7a now, will cordon and drain, move traffic. please wait for :thumbsup: before continuing
prod-support: statuspage draft: "Investigating increased 5xx errors and latency for a subset of requests in us-west. We are performing mitigation; some requests may be degraded." asking for approval to post after next update
sre-lead: go ahead and post that update in 10m unless we have a major rollback. Maria, any risk that kv cache change could cause regressions?
maria: negligible — it's a read window tune only. Rolling it via canary on dev first (2 replicas) then to rack-7 serving instances. If errors drop revert to prior config.
oncall-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledged by jasper
jasper: node-7a drained and restarted serve-rt; no more immediate OOMs on that host. CPU fallback observed and latency stable for requests routed away from rack-7. moving on to node-7b
devon: node-7b modprobe completed, but ib link drops again after 3m on b and then container restarted with CUDA reset. suspect intermittent fabric flapping beyond single NIC — opening ticket with infra network team
sre-lead: good catch. @infra-net please triage physical link and optics on rack-7, escalate to datacenter ops if needed. Also we should prepare an automated runtime mitigation: short-circuit kv sync on severe link error to avoid OOMs in future
prod-support: posted status update. customers notified that we're actively mitigating; will escalate to account teams if errors persist 1h
jasper: handoff to night oncall in 30m. current state: draining in progress, TCP fallback applied to 4/6 nodes, error rate down to 1.6% and falling. leaving playbook steps in thread. handing off to @devon for watch and infra followups
devon: will monitor logs and coordinate with infra. next actions: capture ibstat traces, collect core dumps if driver panics, prepare to repro in staging with synthetic packet loss
sre-lead: thanks team. if any node suddenly flaps again --> trigger full rack failover and shift traffic to other AZ. documenting RCA notes here too and will convert to postmortem if we hit >30m customer impact
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-9821 acknowledged by oncall. Handoff scheduled at 2026-03-15T04:58:00Z
notes: hotfix: kv cache sync window reduced; temporary RDMA->TCP fallback; kernel tuning; node drains; infra escalation and statuspage updates
